shlokas.text: ॐ भद्रं कर्णेभिः श‍ृणुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः । स्थिरैरङ्गैस्तुष्टुवांसस्तनूभिर्व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः ॥ भद्रं नो अपि वातय मनः ॥ ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः । ॥ अथ माण्डूक्योपनिषत् ॥ हरिः ॐ । ॐ इत्येतदक्षरमिदꣳ सर्वं तस्योपव्याख्यानं भूतं भवद् भविष्यदिति सर्वमोङ्कार एव यच्चान्यत् त्रिकालातीतं तदप्योङ्कार एव
shlokas.english_draft: Om! O Gods, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O worshipful ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious. Praising with steady limbs and bodies, may we enjoy the lifespan granted by the gods. May our minds be directed towards the good. Om Peace, Peace, Peace! Om! This syllable OM is all this universe. Its further explanation: all that is past, present, and future is indeed OM. And whatever else transcends the three divisions of time, that too is OM.

shlokas.text: सर्वं ह्येतद् ब्रह्मायमात्मा ब्रह्म सोऽयमात्मा चतुष्पात्
shlokas.english_draft: All this is indeed Brahman. This Self (Atman) is Brahman. This Self has four quarters.

shlokas.text: जागरितस्थानो बहिष्प्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः स्थूलभुग्वैश्वानरः प्रथमः पादः
shlokas.english_draft: The first quarter is Vaishvanara, whose sphere of activity is the waking state, who is conscious of external objects, who has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and who enjoys gross material objects.

shlokas.text: स्वप्नस्थानोऽन्तःप्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः प्रविविक्तभुक्तैजसो द्वितीयः पादः
shlokas.english_draft: The second quarter is Taijasa, whose sphere of activity is the dream state, who is conscious of internal objects, who has seven limbs and nineteen mouths, and who enjoys subtle mental impressions.

shlokas.text: यत्र सुप्तो न कञ्चन कामं कामयते न कञ्चन स्वप्नं पश्यति तत् सुषुप्तम् । सुषुप्तस्थान एकीभूतः प्रज्ञानघन एवानन्दमयो ह्यानन्दभुक् चेतोमुखः प्राज्ञस्तृतीयः पादः
shlokas.english_draft: That state where one sleeping desires no desire and sees no dream is deep sleep (Sushupti). The third quarter is Prajna, whose sphere of activity is deep sleep, in whom all experiences become unified, who is a mass of pure consciousness, full of bliss, enjoying bliss, and the gateway to consciousness.

shlokas.text: एष सर्वेश्वरः एष सर्वज्ञ एषोऽन्तर्याम्येष योनिः सर्वस्य प्रभवाप्ययौ हि भूतानाम्
shlokas.english_draft: This is the Lord of all (Sarveshvara); this is the Knower of all (Sarvajna); this is the Inner Controller (Antaryami); this is the source of all, the origin and dissolution of all beings.

shlokas.text: नान्तःप्रज्ञं न बहिष्प्रज्ञं नोभयतःप्रज्ञं न प्रज्ञानघनं न प्रज्ञं नाप्रज्ञम् । अदृष्टमव्यवहार्यमग्राह्यमलक्षणं अचिन्त्यमव्यपदेश्यमेकात्मप्रत्ययसारं प्रपञ्चोपशमं शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं चतुर्थं मन्यन्ते स आत्मा स विज्ञेयः
shlokas.english_draft: Not conscious of the internal, nor conscious of the external, nor conscious of both, nor a mass of consciousness, nor simple consciousness, nor unconsciousness. Unseen, beyond empirical transactions, ungraspable, without distinctive marks, unthinkable, indescribable, the essence of the sole consciousness of the Self, the cessation of the phenomenon, tranquil, auspicious, non-dual—this they consider the Fourth quarter (Turiya). That is the Self; That is to be realized.

shlokas.text: सोऽयमात्माध्यक्षरमोङ्कारोऽधिमात्रं पादा मात्रा मात्राश्च पादा अकार उकारो मकार इति
shlokas.english_draft: That Self, viewed from the standpoint of the syllable OM, is represented by its sound-measures (matras). The quarters of the Self are the matras of OM, and the matras are the quarters: namely, the letter A, the letter U, and the letter M.

shlokas.text: जागरितस्थानो वैश्वानरोऽकारः प्रथमा मात्राऽऽप्तेरादिमत्त्वाद् वाऽऽप्नोति ह वै सर्वान् कामानादिश्च भवति य एवं वेद
shlokas.english_draft: Vaishvanara, whose sphere is the waking state, is the letter 'A', the first matra, on account of pervasion (apti) or being first (adimattva). He who knows this obtains all desires and becomes the foremost.

shlokas.text: स्वप्नस्थानस्तैजस उकारो द्वितीया मात्रोत्कर्षात् उभयत्वाद्वोत्कर्षति ह वै ज्ञानसन्ततिं समानश्च भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति य एवं वेद
shlokas.english_draft: Taijasa, whose sphere is the dream state, is the letter 'U', the second matra, on account of elevation (utkarsha) or intermediate position (ubhayatva). He who knows this elevates the continuum of knowledge, becomes equal to all, and no one ignorant of Brahman is born in his lineage.

shlokas.text: सुषुप्तस्थानः प्राज्ञो मकारस्तृतीया मात्रा मितेरपीतेर्वा मिनोति ह वा इदं सर्वमपीतिश्च भवति य एवं वेद
shlokas.english_draft: Prajna, whose sphere is deep sleep, is the letter 'M', the third matra, on account of measuring (miti) or merging (apiti). He who knows this measures all this and becomes the place of dissolution.

shlokas.text: अमात्रश्चतुर्थोऽव्यवहार्यः प्रपञ्चोपशमः शिवोऽद्वैत एवमोङ्कार आत्मैव संविशत्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं य एवं वेद
shlokas.english_draft: The partless (amatra) is the Fourth state (Turiya)—unutterable, the cessation of phenomena, auspicious, non-dual. Thus OM is indeed the Self. He who knows this enters the Self through his own self.
